case_name: Sheila Sebastian v. R. Jawaharaj and Another

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Sheila Sebastian ... Appellant
versus
R. Jawaharaj and Another ... Respondents
Coram: N.V. Ramana, S. Abdul Nazeer, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 11 May 2018

RAMANA, J.:
1. This criminal appeal involves the definition of forgery under Section 463 and 'making a false document' under Section 464 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 in relation to an allegedly forged power of attorney.

2. Making of False Document is Sine Qua Non for Forgery: The essential ingredient of forgery under Section 463 is the making of a false document as defined under Section 464 IPC. Unless the accused is proved to have forged the signature or made the document, or caused someone else to make it, he cannot be convicted of forgery under Section 465 or Section 468 IPC.

3. Decision: The prosecution failed to establish that respondent Jawaharaj made or signed the forged power of attorney, although it was registered in his favour. An accused cannot be convicted of forgery simply because he is the beneficiary of a forged document, unless he is shown to be the author or conspirator. Acquittal under Section 468 IPC upheld.
